subject: Discovery Recap + Pilot Charter: scope, KPIs & access runway
messages:
From: Maya Torres <maya.t@arborgrid.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 15:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's discovery call

Thanks again for the call today — appreciate Sofia and Ben walking through Redwood's serving and cost playbook. I wanted to capture the points we discussed and confirm ArborGrid's asks so we can land the pilot charter quickly. Notes below: 

Pain / goals (ArborGrid):
- Current infra: in-house LLM endpoints handle extractive Q&A for clinical triage; cost per 100k tokens is a blocker and we've seen cost overruns on peak days.
- Latency spikes during bursts (90th-95th percentile > 350ms) are causing downstream timeouts in our UI.
- Security & audit: need per-request logging, retention controls, and a quick path for SOC-style evidence.
- Prompt variability: outputs vary across user queries — want guardrails and regression testing for prompt changes.

Pilot ask (what we'd like to validate):
- 30-day pilot scoped to 1 production-like flow (extractive Q&A) using a 100k-record sample.
- Success metrics: 95th percentile latency < 120ms; cost reduction >= 30% vs current baseline; answer accuracy F1 >= 0.82 on our eval set.
- Deliverables: setup in our AWS account, short prompt evaluation harness (20-30 prompt templates), weekly interim readouts, and a short end-of-pilot report with ops recommendations.

Access items we can provision quickly:
- S3 sample bucket (will provide a read-only IAM role or an access key).
- A service account for Redwood to run integration tests and telemetry.
- IP allowlist entries for your staging egress.

Questions / asks to Redwood to finalize pilot charter:
1) Can you confirm owners on the Redwood side and a 4-week timeline broken down by setup / tuning / evaluation / wrap?
2) Any minimum compliance artifacts you need in advance (SOC2 evidence pointer, basic security questionnaire)?
3) Proposed kickoff window — would May 20 or 21 work for a 30–40 minute kickoff + access checklist review?

We can also loop in our security lead (cc'd separately) if you need to coordinate the questionnaire.

Thanks — happy to drive provisioning once we align on the plan.

— Maya
Maya Torres
Head of Product Ops, ArborGrid
maya.t@arborgrid.com

Attachment: s3_sample_manifest.csv (manifest listing 100k sample keys)

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Torres <maya.t@arborgrid.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 16:10:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's discovery call

Hi Maya — great to meet you today and thanks for the clear summary (captured verbatim where possible). Below is a draft pilot charter and a short runway we propose based on the metrics you listed. I've attached an editable draft (pilot-charter-v1.pdf) that we can iterate on.

Proposed pilot charter (summary):
- Scope: extractive Q&A flow, 100k-record sample from your S3 (read-only role).
- Duration: 4 calendar weeks (1 week setup/provisioning + 2 weeks tuning/evals + 1 week wrap + final readout).
- KPIs: 95th pctl latency target 120ms (production-ish traffic), >=30% cost reduction vs your baseline, accuracy threshold F1 >= 0.82.
- Owners (Redwood):
  - Sofia Ivanova (AE) — commercial owner / weekly touchpoint
  - Ben Carter (Solutions Engineering) — technical lead / deployment & kernels
  - Marissa Cole (Customer Success) — success plan, prompt-eval coordination and final report
- What Redwood will deliver: inference runtime tuning, batching/quantization recommendations, prompt-eval harness, weekly telemetry dashboard access, and a final operations playbook.

Pre-kickoff checklist (what we'll need from ArborGrid):
- Read-only IAM role / temporary keys for S3 sample: ideal by EOD May 19.
- Short security questionnaire if you have one (Ben and Marissa will start with the standard matrix; if your security team prefers the XLSX you can attach it).
- Network allowlist (IP ranges or CIDR) for staging egress.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) We (Redwood) share pilot-charter-v1 (attached) and a short runbook link for the kickoff.
2) Kickoff: May 20 at 10:00am ET or May 21 at 9:00am ET — 30–40 minutes to walk owners and confirm access.
3) You provision the read-only S3 and either add our service account or share keys.

I attached the draft charter and a short checklist. Ben — I'll hand to you to call out any technical caveats (model variant suggestions, quantization notes, expected token volumes).

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0126

Attachment: pilot-charter-v1.pdf (editable charter + checklist)

From: Maya Torres <maya.t@arborgrid.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's discovery call

Thanks Sofia — this looks great and aligns with our expectations. We'll do the following this week:
- I'll have our infra team create the read-only role and share an access key (target: Tue EOD, May 19).
- I'll route Redwood's security questionnaire to our SecOps (they prefer to get the XLSX; see placeholder attachment).
- Confirm kickoff: May 20 at 10:00am ET works for us. I'll send a calendar invite and include our security lead (priya.rao@arborgrid.com) for the first 10 minutes.

One note on metrics: our baseline 95th pctl latency is measured at daytime production load; we can share the baseline telemetry prior to kickoff so Ben can size batch/kv cache expectations.

Doc links: SOW draft (attached), security_questionnaire.xlsx (attached).

— Maya

Attachments referenced: security_questionnaire.xlsx, SOW_draft.docx

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's discovery call — pre-kickoff notes

Looping back with a short pre-kickoff tech checklist and internal owner tasks so we're aligned before the May 20 kickoff (calendar shows May 20 confirmed):

Ben's pre-kickoff checklist (technical):
- Confirm S3 access: ensure we get a read-only IAM role with a policy that allows GetObject/ListBucket for the sample prefix. If keys are shared, rotate via a short-lived credential flow.
- Network: grab ArborGrid's allowlist CIDRs — we'll add to staging egress.
- Model & runtime: I'll stand up a quantized variant for initial latency testing (likely 8-bit Q4/INT8 depending on their model). Expect initial warmup tokens; plan continuous batching windows to keep 95th pctl lower.
- Prompt eval set: Marissa, can you assemble 25–30 representative prompts (mix of long clinical notes and short patient queries)? We'll need an eval harness by day 7.
- Telemetry & access: request HubSpot deal link (sofia — please push deal id ARB-2026-1458 into the kickoff notes) and share read-only dashboard to ArborGrid's stakeholders after week 1.

Attachments I'm preparing to bring to kickoff: sg-allowlist.txt (CIDR template), quick-runbook.md (access steps), initial model-variant-readme.md.

Marissa — will you own the prompt/eval pack and weekly success readout? Sofia — I'll ping you once the staging cluster is up so we can calendar the warmup run.

Thanks — excited to get this running.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Attachment references: sg-allowlist.txt, quick-runbook.md
